analysis.investment_thesis: Apollo Techno is a tiny, highly leveraged capital-goods manufacturer (D/E 1.16, debt Rs 33 Cr vs equity Rs 29 Cr) in cyclical construction equipment — the antithesis of the boring, consumer-facing compounder I seek. Despite a good FY25 (revenue Rs 99 Cr, PAT Rs 14 Cr), the multi-year track record is thin and volatile, and the business sits entirely outside my circle of competence.
key_strengths: Promoter holding healthy at 73.05% with FY25 ROE of 73.8% and ROCE 31.2%
Debt being reduced (borrowings down from Rs 43 Cr to Rs 33 Cr in FY25) and OCF turned positive Rs 15 Cr
Revenue CAGR 20.5% (FY21-25) with margins expanding sharply in FY25
key_risks: D/E of 1.16 is unacceptable — more than 3x my comfort ceiling of 0.3
Earnings history erratic: PAT Rs 0 Cr in FY21/22 to Rs 14 Cr in FY25 — one good year, not a pattern
Cyclical construction-equipment play with lumpy order book, operating margin only 7.4%
red_flags: Total debt (Rs 32 Cr) exceeds equity in earlier years; inflated ROE is a low-equity artefact
Negative operating cash flow in FY21 and FY22 — business burnt cash for two of last five years
Zero cash on balance sheet — no liquidity cushion against a downturn
analysis.detailed_analysis:
This is not a business I would touch. I build my portfolio around predictable consumer demand — DMart, retail, FMCG, steady private banks — where I can forecast cash flows a decade out. Apollo Techno sells drilling rigs to infrastructure contractors; demand is entirely tied to the government capex cycle and private construction, which is the opposite of predictable. The 73.8% ROE looks dazzling but is flattered by a tiny equity base of Rs 29 Cr against Rs 32 Cr of debt; strip out leverage and the economics are pedestrian with a 7.4% operating margin.

The balance sheet fails my most basic test. D/E at 1.16 versus my ceiling of 0.3 is a disqualifier on its own, and the company carries virtually no cash. The three-year earnings ramp (PAT of Rs 0, Rs 1, Rs 3, Rs 14 Cr) is encouraging but far too short — I need 10+ years of consistent compounding before I commit capital. P/E of 11 looks cheap, but cheap leveraged cyclicals stay cheap for good reason. Pass without hesitation.
